claim: Lmx1a-/- mice exhibit a ~17% reduction in the length of the hippocampal CA1-3 fields at postnatal day 21 (P21).
source: Extending previous histological studies (Kuwamura et al., 2005; Sekiguchi et al., 1992), we found a modest (~17%) reduction in the length of the hippocampal CA1-3 fields (Figure 1A–C)
evidence: The claim is supported by measurements shown in Figure 1A-C and is directly stated in the text with specific quantification.

claim: Lmx1a-/- mice exhibit a ~55% reduction in the hippocampal fissure (HF) that overlays the DG at P21.
source: we found a modest (~17%) reduction in the length of the hippocampal CA1-3 fields (Figure 1A–C), but a dramatic reduction of the HF that overlays the DG (~55% reduction, Figure 1A, B and D)
evidence: The claim is supported by measurements shown in Figure 1A, B, and D and is directly stated in the text with specific quantification.

claim: Lmx1a-/- mice exhibit a ~78% reduction in the number of DG (Prox1+) neurons at P21.
source: and the number of DG (Prox1+) neurons (~78% reduction, Figure 1E–G) in postnatal day 21 (P21) Lmx1a-/- mice.
evidence: The claim is supported by cell counts shown in Figure 1E-G and is directly stated in the text with specific quantification.

claim: Input resistance is aberrantly low in DG neurons in Lmx1a-/- mice at P21.
source: Input resistance, a major determinant of neuronal excitability (Yang et al., 2021), was aberrantly low in DG neurons in Lmx1a-/- mice (Figure 1H–J).
evidence: The claim is supported by electrophysiological recordings shown in Figure 1H-J and is directly stated in the text.

claim: P3 Lmx1a-/- mutants exhibit intact patterning of the hippocampal subfields.
source: In P3 Lmx1a-/- mutants, Ctip2 immunohistochemistry (Roy et al., 2019) revealed intact patterning of the hippocampal subfields (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A and B)
evidence: The claim is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A and B and is directly stated in the text.

claim: P3 Lmx1a-/- mutants exhibit a reduced number of DG neurons.
source: but already reduced number of DG neurons (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C–E).
evidence: The claim is supported by cell counts shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1C-E and is directly stated in the text.

claim: Fewer Prox1+ DNe cells were detected in Lmx1a-/- mutants at e14.5.
source: Immunohistochemistry with antibodies specific for Prox1, which at e14.5 serves as a marker for DNe (Lavado et al., 2010), revealed the presence of fewer DNe cells in Lmx1a-/- mutants than in their wild-type littermates (Figure 1K–M).
evidence: The claim is supported by cell counts shown in Figure 1K-M and is directly stated in the text.

claim: Proliferation is reduced in the DNe of e14.5 Lmx1a-/- embryos.
source: A short (90 min) BrdU pulse, used to label cells in the S phase of the cell cycle, revealed a reduced proliferation (Figure 1N–Q)
evidence: The claim is supported by BrdU labeling experiments shown in Figure 1N-Q and is directly stated in the text.

claim: There is no difference in the number of apoptotic cells in the DNe of Lmx1a-/- embryos relative to wild-type littermates at e14.5.
source: but immunohistochemistry with antibodies specific for activated Caspase 3 revealed no difference in the number of apoptotic cells in the DNe of Lmx1a-/- embryos relative to their wild-type littermates at this early stage (Figure 1R–T).
evidence: The claim is supported by apoptosis assays shown in Figure 1R-T and is directly stated in the text.

claim: The fimbrial scaffold appeared grossly normal in e18.5 Lmx1a mutants.
source: While the fimbrial scaffold appeared grossly normal, the transhilar scaffold was diminished in e18.5 Lmx1a mutants (Figure 1U–V').
evidence: The claim is supported by GFAP immunostaining shown in Figure 1U-V' and is directly stated in the text.

claim: The transhilar scaffold was diminished in e18.5 Lmx1a mutants.
source: While the fimbrial scaffold appeared grossly normal, the transhilar scaffold was diminished in e18.5 Lmx1a mutants (Figure 1U–V').
evidence: The claim is supported by GFAP immunostaining shown in Figure 1U-V' and is directly stated in the text.

claim: At e16, a larger fraction of migrated BrdU+ cells was located in the DMS and fewer were found in the FDJ in Lmx1a mutants compared to wild-type controls.
source: Compared to wild-type controls, in Lmx1a mutants, a larger fraction of migrated BrdU+ cells was located at the beginning of their migratory route (DMS), and fewer of them were found in the FDJ (Figure 1—figure supplement 2C–E).
evidence: The claim is supported by BrdU migration experiments shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2C-E and is directly stated in the text.

claim: At e18.5, Lmx1a mutants exhibited a larger fraction of migrated BrdU+ cells in the DMS, and smaller fractions of BrdU+ cells in the FDJ and DG regions.
source: Similar to e16, at e18.5, Lmx1a mutants exhibited a larger fraction of migrated BrdU+ cells in the DMS, and smaller fractions of BrdU+ cells in the FDJ and DG regions (Figure 1—figure supplement 2F–H)
evidence: The claim is supported by BrdU migration experiments shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2F-H and is directly stated in the text.

claim: The total number of migrated BrdU+ cells was significantly lower in Lmx1a-/- embryos compared to wild-type controls at e18.5.
source: The total number of migrated BrdU+ cells (i.e., those located in the DMS + FDJ + DG regions) was significantly lower in Lmx1a-/- embryos compared to wild-type controls (Figure 1—figure supplement 2F, G and I)
evidence: The claim is supported by BrdU cell counts shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2F, G, and I and is directly stated in the text.

claim: Proliferation and apoptosis in the CH of Lmx1a mutants are normal.
source: A short BrdU pulse and anti-activated Caspase 3 immunohistochemistry (Ivaniutsin et al., 2009; Miquelajauregui et al., 2007) revealed normal proliferation and apoptosis in the CH of Lmx1a mutants (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by BrdU and apoptosis assays shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1 and is directly stated in the text.

claim: A smaller fraction of progenitors exit the cell cycle in the CH of Lmx1a-/- embryos.
source: In contrast, BrdU/Ki67 immunohistochemistry after a 24 hr BrdU pulse (Chizhikov et al., 2019) revealed a smaller fraction of progenitors exiting the cell cycle in Lmx1a-/- embryos (Figure 2A–C)
evidence: The claim is supported by BrdU/Ki67 co-labeling experiments shown in Figure 2A-C and is directly stated in the text.

claim: Many CR cells were still located at the FDJ surface in e15.5 Lmx1a-/- littermates, which was associated with a reduced HF length.
source: Immunohistochemistry against the CR cell marker Reelin (Hodge et al., 2013; Ledonne et al., 2016; Siegenthaler and Miller, 2008) revealed that in e15.5 wild-type embryos many CR cells have populated the HF and few remained at the FDJ. In contrast, in Lmx1a-/- littermates, many CR cells were still at the FDJ, and the HF was abnormally short (Figure 2D–F).
evidence: The claim is supported by Reelin immunostaining shown in Figure 2D-F and is directly stated in the text.

claim: CR cell distribution and HF abnormalities persisted at P3 in Lmx1a-/- mice.
source: CR cell distribution and HF abnormalities persisted at P3 (Figure 2—figure supplement 2)
evidence: The claim is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2 and is directly stated in the text.

claim: 612 genes were significantly downregulated in the CH of Lmx1a mutants compared to wild-type littermates at e13.5.
source: We found that 612 genes were significantly downregulated, and 457 genes were significantly upregulated in the CH of Lmx1a mutants compared to wild-type littermates (Figure 2G and H).
evidence: The claim is supported by RNAseq analysis shown in Figure 2G and H and is directly stated in the text.

claim: 457 genes were significantly upregulated in the CH of Lmx1a mutants compared to wild-type littermates at e13.5.
source: We found that 612 genes were significantly downregulated, and 457 genes were significantly upregulated in the CH of Lmx1a mutants compared to wild-type littermates (Figure 2G and H).
evidence: The claim is supported by RNAseq analysis shown in Figure 2G and H and is directly stated in the text.

claim: 14 genes specifically or predominantly expressed in the CH were downregulated in Lmx1a mutants.
source: Interestingly, 14 of these genes (~25%) were specifically or predominantly expressed in the CH and were downregulated in Lmx1a mutants (Figure 2H, blue dots, and Figure 2—figure supplement 3), including a previously described CH marker Lmo2 (Mangale et al., 2008) and 13 novel CH markers (Slc17a8, Ccdc3, Adamts1, Galnt14, Camk2a, Arfgef3, Rdh10, Plxnc1, Kdr, Asb4, Slc14a2, Peg3, and Slit3).
evidence: The claim is supported by RNAseq and in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 2H and Figure 2—figure supplement 3 and is directly stated in the text.

claim: Eleven known CR cell-enriched genes were downregulated in the CH of Lmx1a-/- embryos.
source: Eleven known CR cell-enriched genes were downregulated (Car10, Lhx1, Trp73, Cntnap2, Reln, Cdkn1a, Chst8, Spock1, Akap6, Cacna2d2, and Tbr2) and six were upregulated (Tmem163, Sema6a, Lhx5, Lingo1, Edil3, and Mapk8) in the CH of Lmx1a-/- embryos (green dots in Figure 2H).
evidence: The claim is supported by RNAseq analysis shown in Figure 2H and is directly stated in the text.

claim: Six known CR cell-enriched genes were upregulated in the CH of Lmx1a-/- embryos.
source: Eleven known CR cell-enriched genes were downregulated (Car10, Lhx1, Trp73, Cntnap2, Reln, Cdkn1a, Chst8, Spock1, Akap6, Cacna2d2, and Tbr2) and six were upregulated (Tmem163, Sema6a, Lhx5, Lingo1, Edil3, and Mapk8) in the CH of Lmx1a-/- embryos (green dots in Figure 2H).
evidence: The claim is supported by RNAseq analysis shown in Figure 2H and is directly stated in the text.

claim: Knockdown of Lmx1a in the CH resulted in downregulation of seven tested Lmx1a downstream targets identified by RNAseq.
source: In these experiments, we confirmed the downregulation of all seven tested Lmx1a downstream targets, identified by RNAseq, including both CH and CR markers/key developmental genes (see below) (Figure 2—figure supplement 4E–K), supporting an intrinsic function of Lmx1a in the CH.
evidence: The claim is supported by in utero electroporation and qRT-PCR experiments shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 4E-K and is directly stated in the text.

claim: Wnt2b and Wnt9a, both expressed specifically in the CH, were significantly downregulated in Lmx1a-/- mutants.
source: Our RNAseq analysis revealed that two Wnts known to activate canonical Wnt signaling, Wnt2b and Wnt9a, both expressed specifically in the CH, were significantly (FDR < 0.05) downregulated in Lmx1a-/- mutants (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by RNAseq data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1 and is directly stated in the text.

claim: Wnt3a expression was significantly downregulated in the CH of Lmx1a-/- embryos at e14.
source: However, quantification of in situ hybridization signal revealed a significant (p<0.01) downregulation of Wnt3a expression in the CH of Lmx1a-/- embryos at e14 (Figure 3A–C)
evidence: The claim is supported by in situ hybridization quantification shown in Figure 3A-C and is directly stated in the text.

claim: qRT-PCR analysis of LCM-isolated CH confirmed downregulation of Wnt3a in Lmx1a-/- mutants at e14.
source: qRT-PCR analysis of LCM-isolated CH confirmed downregulation of Wnt3a in Lmx1a-/- mutants at this stage (Figure 3D and E).
evidence: The claim is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 3D and E and is directly stated in the text.

claim: Loss of one copy of Lmx1a on the Wnt3a+/- background resulted in reduced expression of Wnt3a in the CH.
source: While Wnt3a expression was normal in the CH of Lmx1a+/- or Wnt3a+/- embryos, loss of one copy of Lmx1a on the Wnt3a+/- background (in Lmx1a+/-;Wnt3a+/- double heterozygous embryos) resulted in a reduced expression of Wnt3a in the CH, providing additional evidence for regulation of Wnt3a expression by Lmx1a (Figure 3E).
evidence: The claim is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 3E and is directly stated in the text.

claim: Knockdown of Lmx1a in the CH resulted in reduced expression of Wnt3a.
source: Knockdown of Lmx1a in the CH resulted in a reduced expression of Wnt3a (Figure 2—figure supplement 4I), supporting an intrinsic role for Lmx1a in regulating Wnt3a expression.
evidence: The claim is supported by in utero electroporation and qRT-PCR experiments shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 4I and is directly stated in the text.

claim: Lmx1a+/-;Wnt3a+/- double heterozygotes exhibited a reduced number of DG neurons at P3.
source: In contrast to wild-type or single-gene heterozygous (Lmx1a+/- or Wnt3a+/-) mice, their double heterozygous Lmx1a+/-;Wnt3a+/- littermates exhibited a reduced number (Figure 3F–J) and input resistance (Figure 3K and L) of DG neurons, and transhilar glial scaffold abnormalities (Figure 3M–O).
evidence: The claim is supported by cell counts shown in Figure 3F-J and is directly stated in the text.

claim: Lmx1a+/-;Wnt3a+/- double heterozygotes exhibited reduced input resistance of DG neurons at P21.
source: In contrast to wild-type or single-gene heterozygous (Lmx1a+/- or Wnt3a+/-) mice, their double heterozygous Lmx1a+/-;Wnt3a+/- littermates exhibited a reduced number (Figure 3F–J) and input resistance (Figure 3K and L) of DG neurons, and transhilar glial scaffold abnormalities (Figure 3M–O).
evidence: The claim is supported by electrophysiological recordings shown in Figure 3K and L and is directly stated in the text.

claim: Lmx1a+/-;Wnt3a+/- double heterozygotes exhibited transhilar glial scaffold abnormalities.
source: In contrast to wild-type or single-gene heterozygous (Lmx1a+/- or Wnt3a+/-) mice, their double heterozygous Lmx1a+/-;Wnt3a+/- littermates exhibited a reduced number (Figure 3F–J) and input resistance (Figure 3K and L) of DG neurons, and transhilar glial scaffold abnormalities (Figure 3M–O).
evidence: The claim is supported by GFAP immunostaining shown in Figure 3M-O and is directly stated in the text.

claim: A reduced number of DG neurons in Lmx1a+/-;Wnt3a+/- double heterozygotes was associated with reduced proliferation in DNe.
source: A reduced number of DG neurons was associated with reduced proliferation in DNe (Figure 3P–R).
evidence: The claim is supported by BrdU proliferation assays shown in Figure 3P-R and is directly stated in the text.

claim: Lmx1a-Cre;Tbr2F/F mice exhibited aberrant accumulation of Reelin+ CR cells at the FDJ, associated with a reduced HF length.
source: Similar to Nestin-Cre;Tbr2F/F mice (Hodge et al., 2013), Lmx1a-Cre;Tbr2F/F mice exhibited aberrant accumulation of Reelin+ CR cells at the FDJ, associated with a reduced HF length (Figure 4—figure supplement 1D–F), supporting the conclusion that Tbr2 acts intrinsically in the CR cell lineage to regulate migration of CR cells and HF/DG morphogenesis.
evidence: The claim is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1D-F and is directly stated in the text.

claim: In e13 wild-type embryos, virtually all Tbr2+ cells located in the marginal zone of CH express p73 and are specified CR cells.
source: Co-immunohistochemistry revealed that in e13 wild-type embryos virtually all Tbr2+ cells located in the marginal zone of CH express a CR marker p73 and, thus, were specified CR cells. In contrast, many Tbr2+ cells in the ventricular and intermediate zones of the CH were p73-negative, presumably representing less differentiated cells (Figure 4—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by co-immunostaining data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2 and is directly stated in the text.

claim: Loss of Lmx1a reduced Tbr2 expression in the e13 CH across all three bins (ventricular, intermediate, and marginal zones), but most significantly in the marginal zone.
source: Consistent with our RNAseq data (Figure 4A), immunohistochemistry revealed that loss of Lmx1a reduced Tbr2 expression in the e13 CH across all three bins, but most significantly in the marginal zone (p<0.001, Figure 4B and C).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunostaining quantification shown in Figure 4B and C and is directly stated in the text.

claim: Expression of Tbr2 in the hippocampal progenitors was not affected in Lmx1a-/- embryos.
source: In contrast, expression of Tbr2 in the hippocampal progenitors was not affected (Figure 4B and D).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunostaining quantification shown in Figure 4B and D and is directly stated in the text.

claim: Knockdown of Lmx1a in the CH resulted in reduced expression of Tbr2.
source: Knockdown of Lmx1a in the CH also resulted in reduced expression of Tbr2 (Figure 2—figure supplement 4J), supporting an intrinsic role for Lmx1a in the regulation of Tbr2 expression.
evidence: The claim is supported by in utero electroporation and qRT-PCR experiments shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 4J and is directly stated in the text.

claim: Lmx1a+/-;Lmx1a-Cre;Tbr2+/F double-gene heterozygous mice revealed aberrant accumulation of Reelin+ CR cells at the FDJ, reduced HF length and transhilar scaffold abnormalities.
source: In contrast to wild-type controls or single-gene heterozygotes (Lmx1a+/- or Lmx1a-Cre;Tbr2+/F, in which one copy of Tbr2 was specifically deleted in CH), their Lmx1a+/-;Lmx1a-Cre;Tbr2+/F double-gene heterozygous littermates revealed aberrant accumulation of Reelin+ CR cells at the FDJ, reduced HF length and transhilar scaffold abnormalities (Figure 4E–F and Figure 4—figure supplement 3).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 4E-F and Figure 4—figure supplement 3 and is directly stated in the text.

claim: These phenotypes in Lmx1a+/-;Lmx1a-Cre;Tbr2+/F mice were not associated with a delayed exit of CH progenitors from the cell cycle.
source: These phenotypes were not associated with a delayed exit of CH progenitors from the cell cycle (Figure 4G and H).
evidence: The claim is supported by BrdU/Ki67 co-labeling experiments shown in Figure 4G and H and is directly stated in the text.

claim: Cdkn1a expression was reduced in the CH of Lmx1a-/- mice at e13.
source: Consistent with our RNAseq analysis (Figure 5A), immunohistochemistry revealed reduced Cdkn1a expression in the CH of Lmx1a-/- mice at e13 (Figure 5B–D).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunostaining quantification shown in Figure 5B-D and is directly stated in the text.

claim: Knockdown of Lmx1a in the CH resulted in reduced expression of Cdkn1a.
source: Knockdown of Lmx1a in the CH resulted in a reduced expression of Cdkn1a (Figure 2—figure supplement 4K), supporting an intrinsic role for Lmx1a in regulating Cdkn1a expression.
evidence: The claim is supported by in utero electroporation and qRT-PCR experiments shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 4K and is directly stated in the text.

claim: Expression of exogenous Cdkn1a in the CH of Lmx1a-/- embryos increased the fraction of progenitors that exited the cell cycle.
source: Expression of exogenous Cdkn1a in the CH of Lmx1a-/- embryos increased the fraction of progenitors that exited the cell cycle (GFP+/Ki67- cells among GFP+ cells), making it comparable to that in controls (CH of wild-type embryos electroporated with GFP alone) (Figure 5E–H).
evidence: The claim is supported by in utero electroporation and immunostaining experiments shown in Figure 5E-H and is directly stated in the text.

claim: Cdkn1a electroporation normalized the number of differentiating (p73+) CR cells in Lmx1a-/- embryos.
source: Interestingly, Cdkn1a electroporation also normalized the number of differentiating (p73+) (Meyer et al., 2004; Siegenthaler and Miller, 2008) CR cells in Lmx1a-/- embryos (Figure 5I–L)
evidence: The claim is supported by in utero electroporation and immunostaining experiments shown in Figure 5I-L and is directly stated in the text.

claim: Lmx1a+GFP electroporation into medial telencephalon induced ectopic Wnt3a and Ccdc3.
source: In contrast to GFP controls, Lmx1a+GFP electroporation into medial telencephalon induced ectopic Wnt3a and Ccdc3. Extensive overlap of GFP expression with Wnt3a and Ccdc3 signals suggested cell-autonomous induction of these genes by Lmx1a in these experiments (Figure 6A–D' and Figure 6—figure supplement 1A–D').
evidence: The claim is supported by in utero electroporation and in situ hybridization experiments shown in Figure 6A-D' and Figure 6—figure supplement 1A-D' and is directly stated in the text.

claim: In Lmx1a-electroporated samples, numerous ectopic p73+ cells were observed deep in the neuroepithelium beyond the CH.
source: In contrast to GFP controls, in Lmx1a-electroporated samples, we observed numerous ectopic p73+ cells deep in the neuroepithelium beyond the CH (Figure 6E–H'), which was associated with a dramatic increase in the total number of p73+ cells (Figure 6E–I).
evidence: The claim is supported by in utero electroporation and immunostaining experiments shown in Figure 6E-I and is directly stated in the text.

claim: Electroporation of Lmx1a resulted in a significant reduction of Lhx2 expression in hippocampal primordium cells.
source: Finally, quantification of the immunohistochemistry signal revealed a significant reduction of Lhx2 expression in hippocampal primordium cells electroporated with Lmx1a+GFP versus those electroporated with GFP alone (Figure 6J–L).
evidence: The claim is supported by in utero electroporation and immunostaining quantification shown in Figure 6J-L and is directly stated in the text.

claim: Electroporation of Lmx1a did not induce expression of the choroid plexus marker Ttr.
source: Notably, electroporation of Lmx1a did not induce expression of the choroid plexus marker Ttr (Figure 6—figure supplement 1E–F').
evidence: The claim is supported by in utero electroporation and immunostaining experiments shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1E-F' and is directly stated in the text.

claim: When electroporated into the lateral cortex, Lmx1a did not induce expression of Wnt3a.
source: Interestingly, when electroporated into the lateral cortex, Lmx1a did not induce expression of Wnt3a (Figure 6—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by in utero electroporation and in situ hybridization experiments shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 2 and is directly stated in the text.

claim: Lmx1a is expressed in the telencephalon limited to dorsal midline structures – the CH and non-neural choroid plexus epithelium (ChPe).
source: LIM-homeodomain transcription factor Lmx1a is one of the earliest markers of the CH. In contrast to the aforementioned genes, its expression in the telencephalon is limited to dorsal midline structures – the CH and non-neural choroid plexus epithelium (ChPe) (Caronia-Brown et al., 2016; Chizhikov et al., 2019; Failli et al., 2002).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Loss of Lmx1a results in an aberrant contribution of the Lmx1a-lineage cells to the hippocampus.
source: Previously, we found that loss of Lmx1a results in an aberrant contribution of the Lmx1a-lineage cells to the hippocampus, suggesting a function of this gene in establishing the CH/hippocampus boundary (Chizhikov et al., 2010).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: The CH is necessary and sufficient for the development of the hippocampus in adjacent neuroepithelium.
source: The CH is necessary and sufficient for the development of the hippocampus in adjacent neuroepithelium (Mangale et al., 2008).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and supported by a citation.

claim: Loss of CH or its signaling molecule Wnt3a leads to the near-complete loss of the hippocampus.
source: Loss of CH or its signaling molecule Wnt3a leads to the near-complete loss of the hippocampus, associated with reduced proliferation in the hippocampal primordium (Lee et al., 2000).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and supported by a citation.

claim: Canonical Wnt signaling from the CH promotes the formation of the transhilar glial scaffold.
source: Canonical Wnt signaling from the CH (involving Wnt3a and likely other Wnts) also promotes the formation of the transhilar glial scaffold, which guides the migration of neural progenitors from the dentate neuroepithelium (DNe) in the ventricular zone to the hippocampal dentate gyrus (DG) (Zhou et al., 2004; Parichha et al., 2022).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and supported by citations.

claim: CR cells form the hippocampal fissure (HF), the sulcus that separates the DG from the CA1 field.
source: In addition to Wnt signaling, CH gives rise to Cajal–Retzius (CR) cells, short-lived neurons that migrate to the hippocampal field, where they form the hippocampal fissure (HF), the sulcus that separates the DG from the CA1 field.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text.

claim: CR cells promote the formation of the transhilar glial scaffold.
source: CR cells also promote the formation of the transhilar glial scaffold (Bielle et al., 2005; Causeret et al., 2021; Hodge et al., 2013; Meyer et al., 2004).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and supported by citations.

claim: Loss of transcription factors Dmrt3/4/5 or Gli3 compromises CH formation.
source: For example, loss of transcription factors Dmrt3/4/5 or Gli3 compromises CH formation (De Clercq et al., 2018; Fotaki et al., 2011; Grove et al., 1998; Kikkawa and Osumi, 2021; Quinn et al., 2009; Saulnier et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and supported by citations.

claim: Lhx2 confers cortical identity in the telencephalic neuroepithelium, cell-autonomously suppressing CH fate.
source: Lhx2 confers cortical identity in the telencephalic neuroepithelium, cell-autonomously suppressing CH fate (Mangale et al., 2008; Monuki et al., 2001).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and supported by citations.

claim: Lmx1a acts as a master regulator to orchestrate the formation and function of the cortical hem (CH).
source: By performing studies in mice, we show that Lmx1a acts as a master regulator to orchestrate the formation and function of the cortical hem (CH), a critical signaling center that controls hippocampus development.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the abstract and is the main conclusion of the study, supported by multiple experiments throughout the manuscript.

claim: Lmx1a co-regulates CH induction, its Wnt signaling, and the differentiation and migration of CH-derived Cajal–Retzius neurons.
source: Lmx1a co-regulates CH induction, its Wnt signaling, and the differentiation and migration of CH-derived Cajal–Retzius neurons.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the abstract and is supported by multiple experiments throughout the manuscript.

claim: Proliferation and, likely, migration abnormalities, but not elevated apoptosis, contribute to DG deficits in Lmx1a-/- mice.
source: Taken together, our data indicate that proliferation and, likely, migration abnormalities, but not elevated apoptosis, contribute to DG deficits in Lmx1a-/- mice.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and is supported by multiple experiments showing reduced proliferation, migration defects, and no change in apoptosis.

claim: Lmx1a is required for normal expression of diverse CH markers and CR cell genes.
source: Thus, Lmx1a is required for normal expression of diverse CH markers and CR cell genes, and our bioinformatics analysis supports the role of Lmx1a in the differentiation and migration of CR cells, and canonical Wnt signaling.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and is supported by RNAseq and bioinformatics analyses.

claim: Lmx1a regulates DG morphogenesis at least partially via secreted Wnts produced in the CH.
source: Canonical Wnt signaling promotes proliferation in the DNe and transhilar scaffold formation (Li and Pleasure, 2005; Zhou et al., 2004; Parichha et al., 2022), suggesting a hypothesis that Lmx1a regulates DG morphogenesis at least partially via secreted Wnts produced in the CH.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that Wnt signaling promotes DG development and that Lmx1a regulates Wnt expression in the CH.

claim: Lmx1a promotes DG development, at least partially, by modulating expression of Wnt3a.
source: Although these double heterozygote experiments alone do not necessarily show that one gene acts via the other, as two genes may act via parallel pathways, reduced expression of Wnt3a in Lmx1a-/- embryos and downregulation of Wnt3a expression in Lmx1a+/-;Wnt3a+/- embryos relative to Wnt3a+/- embryos show that Lmx1a acts upstream of Wnt3a, thus, suggesting that Lmx1a promotes DG development, at least partially, by modulating expression of Wnt3a.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and is supported by gene expression and genetic interaction experiments.

claim: Tbr2 acts intrinsically in the CR cell lineage to regulate migration of CR cells and HF/DG morphogenesis.
source: Similar to Nestin-Cre;Tbr2F/F mice (Hodge et al., 2013), Lmx1a-Cre;Tbr2F/F mice exhibited aberrant accumulation of Reelin+ CR cells at the FDJ, associated with a reduced HF length (Figure 4—figure supplement 1D–F), supporting the conclusion that Tbr2 acts intrinsically in the CR cell lineage to regulate migration of CR cells and HF/DG morphogenesis.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and is supported by conditional knockout experiments shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1D-F.

claim: Lmx1a modulates Tbr2 expression to promote migration of CR cells and HF/transhilar glial scaffold formation.
source: Taken together with reduced expression of Tbr2 in the Lmx1a-/- CH, these data suggest that Lmx1a modulates Tbr2 expression to promote migration of CR cells and HF/transhilar glial scaffold formation.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and is supported by gene expression and genetic interaction experiments.

claim: Decreased Cdkn1a expression contributes to both reduced cell cycle exit in CH and decreased differentiation of CR cells in Lmx1a-/- embryos.
source: indicating that decreased Cdkn1a expression contributes to both reduced cell cycle exit in CH and decreased differentiation of CR cells in Lmx1a-/- embryos.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and is supported by rescue experiments using in utero electroporation of Cdkn1a.

claim: Lmx1a expression specifically induces key CH features in the medial telencephalic neuroepithelium.
source: Thus, Lmx1a expression specifically induces key CH features in the medial telencephalic neuroepithelium.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and is supported by in utero electroporation experiments showing induction of Wnt3a, Ccdc3, CR cells, and downregulation of Lhx2 in the medial telencephalon.

claim: Lmx1a is the first intrinsic molecule that specifies CH fate.
source: This study identifies Lmx1a as the first intrinsic molecule that specifies CH fate and, to our knowledge, provides the strongest example that the orchestration of signaling center development in the CNS utilizes master regulatory genes.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the Discussion and is supported by the gain-of-function experiments showing that Lmx1a is sufficient to induce CH features.

claim: The CH identity is actively assigned by Lmx1a.
source: However, our overexpression of Lmx1a in the hippocampal primordium at e10.75, after the cortical neuroepithelium identity has already been assigned by Lhx2 (Mangale et al., 2008), resulted in cell-autonomous ectopic expression of a CH signaling molecule Wnt3a, a CH marker Ccdc3, and the generation of ectopic p73+ CR cells, indicating that the CH identity is actively assigned by Lmx1a.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and is supported by in utero electroporation experiments.

claim: Medially expressed competence factors (permissive genes) are needed to maintain the CH-inducing activity of Lmx1a.
source: Interestingly, while Lmx1a induced CH features in the medial telencephalon, Lmx1a overexpression in the lateral cortex failed to induce ectopic expression of Wnt3a, indicating that medially expressed competence factors (permissive genes) are needed to maintain the CH-inducing activity of Lmx1a.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that Lmx1a induces CH features in the medial but not lateral telencephalon.

claim: An intrinsic molecule(s) activated by low levels of Bmp signaling acts partially redundant to Lmx1a to assign CH fate in the medial telencephalic neuroepithelium.
source: Thus, it is likely that an intrinsic molecule(s) activated by low levels of Bmp signaling acts partially redundant to Lmx1a to assign CH fate in the medial telencephalic neuroepithelium.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that the CH is not completely lost in Lmx1a-/- mice and from previous studies on Bmp signaling in CH development.

claim: Lmx1a is a novel regulator of proliferation of DG progenitors, hippocampal glial scaffold formation, and electrophysiological properties (input resistance) of DG neurons.
source: Our gene expression studies and phenotypic analysis of Lmx1a-/- mutant and Lmx1a+/-;Wnt3a+/-double heterozygous mice identified Lmx1a as a novel regulator of proliferation of DG progenitors, hippocampal glial scaffold formation, and electrophysiological properties (input resistance) of DG neurons, which likely, at least partially, promotes hippocampal development by modulating Wnt signaling, particularly expression of its secreted ligand Wnt3a.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and is supported by multiple experiments throughout the manuscript.

claim: CR cell differentiation and migration are regulated by Lmx1a via different downstream mediators.
source: Interestingly, despite a delayed migration of CR cells, exit of progenitors from the cell cycle was normal in the CH of Lmx1a+/-; Lmx1a-Cre;Tbr2+/F mice (Figure 4G–H), indicating that CR cell differentiation and migration are regulated by Lmx1a via different downstream mediators.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and is supported by experiments showing that Tbr2 affects CR migration but not cell cycle exit.

claim: Lmx1a promotes differentiation of CR cells at least partially via regulating the exit of their progenitors from the cell cycle via Cdkn1a.
source: Together, our data indicate that Lmx1a promotes differentiation of CR cells at least partially via regulating the exit of their progenitors from the cell cycle via Cdkn1a.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and is supported by rescue experiments using in utero electroporation of Cdkn1a.

claim: A reduced proliferation in the DNe of Lmx1a-/- mutants likely contributes to the reduction of their DG size.
source: Although a reduced proliferation in the DNe of Lmx1a-/- mutants likely contributes to the reduction of their DG size, DNe proliferation abnormalities alone are unlikely to explain the relative change in the fractions of BrdU-labeled cells found in different segments of the migratory route in Lmx1a-/- embryos
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and is supported by proliferation and migration experiments.

claim: A severe disruption of the transhilar glial scaffold is consistent with the presence of migration abnormalities in Lmx1a-/- mutant mice.
source: A severe disruption of the transhilar glial scaffold, the structure necessary for cellular migration from the DNe to the DG, is also consistent with the presence of migration abnormalities in Lmx1a-/- mutant mice.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and is supported by observations of transhilar scaffold defects and migration abnormalities.

claim: The reduced number of Prox1+ DG progenitors in Lmx1a-/- embryos likely results not only from their reduced proliferation but also because of their decreased specification.
source: Thus, although not directly tested in the current study, it is likely that the reduced number of Prox1+ DG progenitors in Lmx1a-/- embryos results not only from their reduced proliferation but also because of their decreased specification.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that Wnt3a, which is downregulated in Lmx1a-/- mice, is known to promote both proliferation and specification of DG progenitors.

claim: Lmx1a has an intrinsic role in the segregation of the CH lineage from cortical (hippocampal) cells.
source: Our current observation that Lmx1a is sufficient to downregulate Lhx2 in e10.75–e12.5 cortical neuroepithelium (Figure 6J–L) indicates an intrinsic role for Lmx1a in the segregation of the CH lineage from cortical (hippocampal) cells.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and is supported by in utero electroporation experiments showing downregulation of Lhx2.

claim: In addition to Lhx2, Lmx1a regulates CH/hippocampus segregation via adhesion genes.
source: Interestingly, our RNAseq analysis revealed significant enrichment in cell–cell and cell–extracellular matrix adhesion pathways among genes misregulated in the Lmx1a-/- CH, suggesting that in addition to Lhx2, Lmx1a regulates CH/hippocampus segregation via adhesion genes.
evidence: The claim is inferred from RNAseq pathway analysis showing enrichment of adhesion-related genes.

claim: Abnormal cell adhesion contributes to aberrant dispersion of Lmx1a-lineage cells into the adjacent hippocampus in Lmx1a mutants.
source: Finally, GO enrichment, GSEA, and GSEA for KEGG analyses predicted compromised cell–cell and cell–extracellular matrix adhesion in Lmx1a-/- CH (Figure 2I, J and L, related processes are highlighted in blue), suggesting that abnormal cell adhesion contributes to previously reported aberrant dispersion of Lmx1a-lineage cells into the adjacent hippocampus in Lmx1a mutants (Chizhikov et al., 2010).
evidence: The claim is inferred from bioinformatics analysis of RNAseq data and previous observations of aberrant cell dispersion.

claim: Genes identified as misexpressed in Lmx1a-/- CH by RNAseq analysis likely include additional important regulators of CH development or mediators of CH function.
source: It is likely that genes identified as misexpressed in Lmx1a-/- CH by our RNAseq analysis include additional important regulators of CH development or mediators of CH function, and further studies are required to fully characterize an Lmx1a-dependent network.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the large number of genes identified as misregulated in the RNAseq analysis.

claim: The development and function of the CH employs Lmx1a as a master regulatory gene.
source: Regardless, our work revealed that the development and function of the CH, a key signaling center in the mammalian brain, employs Lmx1a as a master regulatory gene and established the framework for characterizing the mechanisms that regulate the development and function of signaling centers in the CNS.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and is the main conclusion of the study.
